states.claim: device is a pointer returned by btrfs_find_device_by_devspec; on success it refers to a btrfs_device object, on error it is an ERR_PTR value.
states.evidence:
L18: device = btrfs_find_device_by_devspec(fs_info, devid, device_path);
L20: if (IS_ERR(device)) {

states.claim: device is removed from the alloc list and its fs_devices rw_devices count is decremented while holding chunk_mutex.
device is removed from the device list under device_list_mutex, and cur_devices is set to device->fs_devices.
device is closed and freed after synchronize_rcu.
cur_devices is closed and freed when its open_devices count reaches zero.
On error_undo, device is re-added to the alloc list and its fs_devices rw_devices count is incremented while holding chunk_mutex.

values.claim: num_devices is initialized to the device count returned by btrfs_num_devices(fs_info).
btrfs_check_raid_min_devices is called with num_devices - 1, so the argument is one less than the current device count.
num_devices is reassigned to the superblock device count minus 1 and then written back to the superblock.
If cur_devices differs from fs_devices, fs_devices->total_devices is also decremented by one.
If the device is marked missing, cur_devices->missing_devices is decremented by one.
If device->bdev is non-NULL, cur_devices->open_devices is decremented by one.
After device removal, if cur_devices->open_devices equals 0, the seed list entry is removed and cur_devices is closed and freed.
If the device is writeable, fs_info->fs_devices->rw_devices is decremented by one.
If the device is writeable and fs_info->fs_devices->rw_devices equals 1, removal is rejected with BTRFS_ERROR_DEV_ONLY_WRITABLE.
On error_undo for a writeable device, device->fs_devices->rw_devices is incremented by one.

executions.claim: After btrfs_find_device_by_devspec returns, continuing past the IS_ERR check implies device is a valid non-error pointer; if device_path is non-NULL and equals "missing" with -ENOENT, the error path is taken.
Continuing past the swapfile check implies device is not pinned by an active swapfile.
Continuing past the replace-target check implies BTRFS_DEV_STATE_REPLACE_TGT is not set on device.
Continuing past the only-writable check implies it is not the case that device is writeable and fs_info->fs_devices->rw_devices == 1.
If device is writeable, then before btrfs_shrink_device is called, device is removed from dev_alloc_list and fs_info->fs_devices->rw_devices is decremented under chunk_mutex.
After btrfs_shrink_device returns, if ret is nonzero execution jumps to error_undo; otherwise btrfs_reada_remove_dev is called and execution continues.
After btrfs_rm_dev_item returns, if ret is nonzero execution jumps to error_undo; otherwise execution continues to clear BTRFS_DEV_STATE_IN_FS_METADATA and cancel scrub.
cur_devices is set to device->fs_devices; if cur_devices differs from fs_devices, fs_devices->total_devices is decremented.
If BTRFS_DEV_STATE_MISSING is set on device, cur_devices->missing_devices is decremented.
If device->bdev is non-NULL, cur_devices->open_devices is decremented and the sysfs entry is removed.
If BTRFS_DEV_STATE_WRITEABLE is set on device, btrfs_scratch_superblocks is called with device->bdev and device->name->str before closing the bdev.
After btrfs_free_device, if cur_devices->open_devices == 0, cur_devices is removed from seed_list, closed, and freed.
In error_undo, if BTRFS_DEV_STATE_WRITEABLE is set on device, device is re-added to fs_devices->alloc_list and device->fs_devices->rw_devices is incremented under chunk_mutex.
